title: TRIM vs CLEAN: the import-cleanup pair (and what both miss)
meta_desc: TRIM vs CLEAN for dirty imported data: spaces vs nonprintable characters, the nonbreaking-space gap both miss, and the full cleanup chain.
intro: Pasted and imported text carries invisible junk that breaks lookups and duplicates 'identical' values. TRIM and CLEAN each remove a different kind — and the most common web-import culprit, the nonbreaking space, slips past BOTH.

cols: Leading/trailing spaces + collapses internal runs to one
Whatever you tell it — the gap-filler
Removes nothing — DIAGNOSES by revealing char codes

when.use_when: First resort whenever lookups mysteriously miss or 'duplicates' won't dedupe — stray spaces cause most of it.
Data from old systems or binary-ish exports showing boxes/garbage glyphs, or when in-cell line breaks need flattening.
Web-pasted data: =TRIM(CLEAN(SUBSTITUTE(A2,CHAR(160)," "))) handles all three kinds in one pass — the order (SUBSTITUTE inside, TRIM outside) matters so converted nbsp-spaces get collapsed too.

compat_note: All four execute identically in every version of all three apps we test. Diagnose before cleaning: LEN(A2)-LEN(TRIM(A2)) counts suspect spaces, and CODE(MID(A2,k,1)) at the failing position names the exact culprit — 160 means nonbreaking space, and only SUBSTITUTE will save you.
